reading.body:
H.R. 9442, the Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act, has 20 cosponsors and every one of them is a Democrat. The sponsor is Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and the cosponsor list runs from James McGovern and Maxine Waters to Rashida Tlaib, Summer Lee and Greg Casar. A moratorium bill on AI data centers is, in this Congress, a one-party document.

The bill's own text is tagged with energy and data centers, and it uses preemption language about state law. That combination is the point. A moratorium on data center construction is a direct intervention in the physical layer of AI, the buildings and the power contracts that determine how much compute can actually be trained and served. Preemption language about state law means the bill also touches the question of who sets the rules for siting and electricity, which is where the grid constraint on AI scaling currently lives.

Three lobbying filings from 2025 or later name the bill. Two are from NETWORK, one from the Business Software Alliance. A filing that names a bill shows the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken on it, so these three records establish that the bill has entered the lobbying conversation without saying whether either organization supports or opposes it.

What the data does not cover is the bill's fate. It records a latest status date of 2026-06-24 and no recorded votes, so there is no evidence here of committee action, floor action, or whether the moratorium has any path to becoming law. The cosponsor count measures support among House Democrats, not support in the House.

summary: H.R. 9442, Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act. Latest status date 2026-06-24. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: energy and data centers. Its text uses preemption language about state law. 3 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
